indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.4.2.2: (Document prints '4.2.2' — missing 'B1.' prefix. Full code should be B1.4.2.2.)
indicator.objective: Know examples of common electronic devices and their uses

skills.description: State the use of a given electronic device
Match a device to its use or to a picture
Recognise simple differences between two electronic devices

misconceptions: All electronic devices do the same thing.
A wrist watch is not electronic.
A phone is only for calling.

questions.stem: Which of these is an electronic device?
hints: You use it to call people.
It has a screen and buttons.
questions.explanation: A mobile phone is an electronic device.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any object is an electronic device.

questions.stem: What do we use a camera for?
questions.explanation: A camera is used to take pictures.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the camera with a phone.

questions.stem: Which device do we use to call someone far away?
hints: You put it to your ear.
questions.explanation: We use a phone to call someone far away.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a torch is used for calling.

questions.stem: Which of these is a small electronic device you wear on your wrist?
questions.explanation: A wrist watch is an electronic device worn on the wrist to tell the time.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider a watch electronic.

questions.stem: Which of these devices gives light?
hints: You use it in the dark.
questions.explanation: A torch is an electronic device that gives light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a radio gives light.

questions.stem: Match the device to its use: What is a torch used for?
questions.explanation: A torch is used to give light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may match the torch with calling.

questions.stem: Which device is used to take pictures?
questions.explanation: A camera is used to take pictures.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse a camera with a torch.

questions.stem: What is the main use of a radio?
options: To listen to news and music
questions.explanation: A radio is used to listen to news and music.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a radio is for watching videos.

questions.stem: Which of these is an electronic device?
questions.explanation: A wrist watch is an electronic device.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think natural or simple wooden objects are electronic.

questions.stem: How is a phone different from a camera?
options: A phone can call and take pictures, a camera only takes pictures
A camera can call and take pictures, a phone only takes pictures
hints: Can you make a call with a camera?
What can a phone do besides taking pictures?
questions.explanation: A phone can make calls and take pictures, while a camera is mainly for taking pictures.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a phone is only for calling.

questions.stem: Which device would you use to calculate numbers?
hints: It has numbers and a screen.
questions.explanation: A calculator is an electronic device used for calculating numbers.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a radio can calculate.

questions.stem: Match the device to its use: Which device is used for listening to music?
questions.explanation: A radio is used for listening to music and news.
questions.misconception: Pupils may match the camera with music.

questions.stem: Why is a mobile phone called an electronic device?
options: Because it uses electricity and chips to work
Because it is made of wood
hints: It has a screen and circuits inside.
questions.explanation: A mobile phone is an electronic device because it uses electricity and electronic components (chips) to work.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think phones work by magic.

questions.stem: Ama wants to take a picture of her family. Which device should she use?
questions.explanation: Ama should use a camera to take a picture of her family.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a torch can take pictures.

questions.stem: Which of these devices can be used to call and send messages?
hints: It has a keypad or touchscreen.
questions.explanation: A mobile phone can be used to call and send messages.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize phones do more than just call.

questions.stem: Kwame says 'A torch is not an electronic device.' Is he right?
options: No, it has a bulb and uses electricity
Yes, it is only a light
No, it is a piece of wood
questions.explanation: Kwame is not right. A torch is an electronic device because it has a bulb and uses electricity from a battery.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think torches are too simple to be electronic.

questions.stem: Which device is used to watch cartoons?
hints: You sit in front of it.
questions.explanation: A television is used to watch cartoons and other programmes.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a camera is used to watch cartoons.

questions.stem: If you want to know the time, which device is best?
hints: You wear it on your arm.
questions.explanation: A wrist watch is the best device to tell the time.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the watch with a calculator.

questions.stem: Why is a camera different from a radio?
options: A camera takes pictures and a radio plays sound
A camera plays sound and a radio takes pictures
questions.explanation: A camera is for taking pictures, and a radio is for listening to sound (news/music).
questions.misconception: Pupils may mix up the functions.

questions.stem: Which of these is an electronic device that helps us see in the dark?
hints: It gives a beam of light.
You use it during a power outage.
questions.explanation: A torch is an electronic device that gives light to help us see in the dark.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a camera helps us see in the dark.
